They're joined by the word and, not the word or. So even before we get to the rule of the last antecedent, there is commonly accepted grammatical interpretation. The plain meaning is that those two items would go together and that therefore applicable, if applicable, would have to apply to both. Mr. Gilligan's argument that the insurance company somehow has an obligation to keep asking if the owner intended to make the request that was written down and signed by the owner is not an obligation that I'm aware of under contract law. Certainly, Mr. Gilligan or Mrs. McIntosh have not pled mistake in entering into the contract. And that's the only basis that I'm aware of whereby a party can say, if they fill out the incorrect amount for face value and that amount was actually put into effect, they could turn around and say, that was a mistake, we'd like to rescind it.
